prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a foreground counter running from the bottom-left to the middle-right at roughly 0.4–1.5 m from the camera wearer, with a stack of paper bags on the far left (~0.5–0.7 m), a POS monitor and card reader in the left-center foreground (~0.6–0.9 m), and a clerk standing behind the counter at about 1.2–1.6 m against a back wall and overhead menu boards at 2.5–4.0 m. In frame 1, two other people stand on the far right at roughly 1.5–2.2 m (one ~0.4 m behind the other, both facing left and partly cropped by the right frame edge), before moving out of view as the camera wearer turns left and leans slightly closer to the counter in frames 2–5. Across frames 1–3, the clerk faces the camera wearer while extending his left arm forward to place a small carton onto the right side of the glass counter (~1.0 m away, within both his and the camera wearer's reach) and reaching his right arm toward the paper bags on the left in frames 2–4, while in frame 5 the camera wearer's own left hand enters the bottom-left foreground at ~0.3–0.4 m holding a card next to the card reader. The depth map makes continuous metric distance gradients along the receding glass counter and the forward protrusion of the clerk's outstretched left arm in frame 3 much clearer than in the RGB image alone. However, the map is unreliable on transparent and reflective surfaces, rendering the glass pastry case as a solid opaque ramp that hides the pastries inside, and saturating the nearby paper bags in frames 2–5 into flat white silhouettes with lost surface detail.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates discrete foreground entities against a black background, locating the clerk behind the counter at ~1.2–1.6 m, two people on the far right in frame 1 at ~1.5–2.2 m (with the nearer person in a dark shirt partially occluding the person behind him), and several small counter items between 0.6 m and 1.8 m. It tracks the clerk's upper body (truncated at the waist by the counter occlusion) as he faces toward the camera wearer, holds a small carton up to his left in frames 1–2, sets it down near a bottle on the right counter in frame 3 (~1.0–1.2 m away), reaches right toward the bags in frame 4, and shifts left behind the POS screen (~0.8 m) in frame 5. The map highlights individual small objects and their relative positions—such as the held carton, the bottle and bowls on the counter top, and clusters of pastries inside the lower-right display case—that visually blend into the cluttered background in the RGB strip. However, the segmentation is highly unreliable in class labeling and temporal consistency: it misclassifies the drink carton as a 'remote' (frame 1) and 'cell phone' (frame 2), the POS monitor as a 'laptop' or 'tv', the card reader as a 'mouse' (frame 3), and a machine behind the counter as a 'person' (frame 5). It also completely misses the tall paper bags on the left, the entire counter structure, and the camera wearer's hand holding the card at ~0.3 m in the bottom-left of frame 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely blank across all five frames, detecting only a single magenta hand skeleton in the upper-center of frame 2 and failing to render any yellow body skeletons or other hands. In frame 2, that lone magenta cluster locates the clerk's raised left hand at roughly 1.1–1.2 m from the camera wearer, positioned above the counter and to the right of the clerk's head as he holds the small carton within his arm's reach. Where present in frame 2, the articulated finger keypoints show the exact 3D curl and orientation of the clerk's hand gripping the carton more explicitly than the low-resolution RGB crop. However, the pose map is severely unreliable throughout the sequence, missing the clerk's entire torso, head, and arms in all five frames despite his upper body facing the camera wearer in clear view at 1.2–1.6 m, as well as his right hand resting near the POS terminal (~0.9 m) and reaching toward the bags. It also fails to detect the two partially occluded people standing at 1.5–2.2 m on the right edge of frame 1 and the camera wearer's own left hand entering at ~0.3–0.4 m in the bottom-left of frame 5.
